App.name: Learn the Qur'an
App.description: Understand the Qur'an word by word: hear a real imam, learn each word's meaning, root, and why it ends in fathah, dammah or kasrah — explained simply, sourced from named kitabs.

Home.heading: Understanding Al-Fatihah, word by word
Home.intro: Listen to the imam, then learn each word's meaning, its root, and why it ends in fathah, dammah or kasrah. Explained simply, sourced from named kitabs.
Home.p1_body: Qur'anic verses are only ever heard from a human reciter. The AI voice only explains, in Indonesian, and never recites an ayah.
Home.p2_body: Every meaning, i'rab note, tafsir point and hadith is quoted from a named kitab or dataset, with its reference.
Home.p3_body: Lessons go live only after an ustadz reviews them. During the beta some material is still a draft and is clearly marked.
Home.fatihah_meta: 7 ayat · 29 words · ~3 weeks at 10 minutes a day
Home.next_body: After Al-Fatihah: Al-Ikhlas, An-Nas, Al-Falaq, Al-'Asr, Al-Kawthar and An-Nasr.

Footer.disclaimer: AI-assisted, not an authoritative fatwa. Explanations are drawn from named kitabs and reviewed by an ustadz before going live.

Credits.title: Sources & licences
Credits.intro: This module is built on the works and data below. We credit each source as its licence requires, and we do not store reciters' recordings on our servers: recitation streams directly from the provider.
Credits.streaming_note: When you play a recitation, your browser fetches the audio directly from the recording provider's servers abroad, so your IP address is visible to them.

Surah.draft_banner: Beta: the word meanings, i'rab and notes on this page are drafts awaiting an ustadz's review. The ayah text and the imam's recitation themselves are unchanged.

Lesson.words_intro: Tap a word in the recitation above to hear it again. Below: its meaning, root, and why it ends the way it does.

Word.sharaf_heading: Sharaf: how the word is formed
Word.sharaf_forms_note: Word forms (tashrif), not quotations of an ayah.

Player.hint_tap: Tap a word to hear it alone. Want gaps to repeat after the imam? Choose Al-Husary's teaching recitation (Mu'allim).

Exercise.score: {right} of {total} right on the first try. Repeat any time — repetition is how memory sticks.
Exercise.tap_instruction: Play the imam's voice, then tap the word he recites.
Exercise.why_instruction: Choose the reason this word ends with that vowel.
Exercise.sort_instruction: Tap a word, then tap its case: marfū' (▲), manshūb (◆), majrūr (▼) or mabnī (■).
Exercise.role_instruction: Choose each word's role in this ayah.
Exercise.wazn_instruction: From the root and its pattern family, pick the right form for each label.
Exercise.wazn_note: These are Arabic word forms (tashrif), not quotations of an ayah.

Concept.index_intro: Each concept is explained once here, then reused in every ayah and surah where it appears.

Guided.title: Guided lesson
Guided.ready: Press Start: the imam recites the ayah, then each word is recited and explained. You can pause at any time.
Guided.captions_note: Explanations show as text for now; the spoken narration follows. The ayah is always recited by the imam.
Guided.intro: Listen to the imam recite ayah {n}.
Guided.practice: Your turn: do the practice below, then continue.
Guided.recap: Listen to the whole ayah once more, and recite along with the imam.
